rationale: Choose structure as a testable design without generated history, not an empirically ranked winner. The original 25-heavy-atom bound ligand supplies the Hungarian coordinate anchor; the original receptor crop supplies the registered 2 A repulsion target. Neither requires generated Steer coordinates, affinity weights or parent-child increments. A real bound conformation avoids independently averaged feature targets; registered multimodal fields remain alternatives for preserving distinct selected conformations. Endpoint enrichment motivates coordinate hypotheses, but missing landmark mappings prevent converting regional associations into executable targets here. Landmark 00 increment support does not supply a coordinate displacement target, so no increment-matching term is added. Contact weight zero avoids inferring affinity from generic proximity; repulsion weight two is a proposed clash-control tradeoff, not an estimated optimum. Keep native_rms_ratio 0.33 and the matched execution contract, with time_ramp_power zero because stage-specific evidence is absent. Use FLOWR endpoint VJP with detached Hungarian correspondence. Component weights change direction; whole-scalar rescaling may cancel under gradient normalization. Evaluate final predicted pIC50 and strain against registered historical alternatives.
failure_modes: A single bound-ligand template can suppress legitimate alternative conformations or distort candidates after graph transitions.
Untyped 2 A repulsion cannot represent element-specific sterics or physical binding energy.
Detached Hungarian correspondence can change discontinuously; atom-count changes can weaken anchor comparability.
Chosen component weights lack executed ablation support and may trade predicted pIC50 improvement for strain.
Selected enrichment evidence and nonsignificant adjusted survival effects do not establish causal or durable benefit; one generation seed cannot resolve outcome uncertainty.
